data.description:
## Description

Update all 10 code-reviewer-*.md agent files to include `verification_evidence` in their finding JSON schema and add a guidance paragraph explaining when and how to emit it.

The field is required only on findings that make an absence claim (language matching the anchor list defined by S1). When a finding asserts something "is not present", "does not exist", "is missing", etc., the agent must run a grep/stat/path-resolve command and capture the output as evidence.

## Done Definitions

- All 10 code-reviewer-*.md files contain `"verification_evidence"` in their finding JSON schema (alongside `cited_excerpt`)
- Each agent has a guidance paragraph (placed after the `cited_excerpt` guidance) explaining: when to emit (absence claims only), the format `{"command": "...", "output": "..."}`, and that the command output is the evidentiary anchor for the verifier agent
- Running `tests/agents/test-verification-evidence-emission.sh` exits 0 (GREEN) after this task
- No changes to code-reviewer-arbiter.md (out of scope for S2)

## File Impact

- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-light.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-standard.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-performance.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-deep-arch.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-deep-correctness.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-deep-hygiene.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-deep-verification.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-security-red-team.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-security-blue-team.md` — UPDATED
- `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-test-quality.md` — UPDATED

## Testing Mode

GREEN — makes T1 tests pass

## Implementation Notes

Add to finding JSON schema in each agent (after `cited_excerpt`, before `reachability`):
```json
"verification_evidence": {"command": "<shell command run to verify the absence claim>", "output": "<exact command output>"}
```

Add guidance paragraph after the `cited_excerpt` guidance block:

> **verification_evidence** — required when the finding makes an absence claim. Absence language includes: "is not present", "does not exist", "is missing", "no X found", "never defined", "lacks", etc. When your finding uses such language, you MUST run a shell command (grep, stat, ls, or path-resolve) to confirm the absence and capture the output. Set `command` to the exact command run and `output` to the exact terminal output. If the command confirms existence rather than absence, the claim is a false positive — drop the finding instead of emitting it. Omit this field on findings that make no absence claims.

Note: The `verification_evidence` field maps to the schema contract defined in S1. During soft-deprecation mode (before S1's sentinel file is created), the validator emits warnings rather than errors for missing evidence on absence-claim findings.
